candidates.title: Flag missing signatures and invoice mismatches

demandEvidence.chore: Review customer documents for missing signatures or invoice totals that differ from order amounts, then prepare a correction request.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The PDF does not contain your signature

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable exception note that identifies a missing signature or an invoice total mismatch and drafts a customer follow-up.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one synthetic or authorized test document record for review.
steps: Compare the invoice total with the order amount.
Mark any discrepancy and show the values used.
Draft a short follow-up from an operator-approved template.
Require a person to verify and send the request.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On test records containing either named discrepancy, the note flags the correct condition and includes no unsupported customer or invoice facts.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies authorized or synthetic inputs, confirms whether a document is actually incomplete, checks every proposed request, and sends it; the prototype must not decide payment or legal validity.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports document extraction or comparison.
Actual document formats, customer data access, repeat frequency, and willingness to pay are unknown.
No external message sending or invoice persistence is established.

ease.reason: A beginner can test two explicit exception rules on synthetic fields; document extraction and real shop access are unsupported.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online sellers may pay for preparing exception follow-ups; the post establishes neither purchase intent nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare supplied totals and a signature flag, but real document formats and extraction accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed rules can flag supplied discrepancies and draft text, but the source documents no automation and a person must verify and send each request.

evidence.reason: The fresh post gives two concrete customer-document discrepancy examples, but no frequency, workflow detail, corroboration, or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: The source supports two concrete exception types and a bounded synthetic-input experiment. The provisional mean is 4.6, below the 6 threshold; no implementation capability or paying customer is established.

candidates.title: Prepare a safe workflow repair checklist

demandEvidence.chore: Plan a bounded repair that restores one missing workflow node and its two connections while protecting the other workflow settings and identity.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Only the missing node and its two connections should be restored.

experimentPlan.output: A review checklist comparing a supplied before-state, intended node and connections, and proposed after-state for an inactive test workflow.
inputs: Synthetic intended node and connection description
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a fictional or authorized inactive-workflow repair scenario and its stated invariants.
steps: List the expected nodes and connections from the supplied description.
Compare the proposed state with the supplied before-state.
Flag changes outside the requested node and connections.
Check that listed identity and settings invariants are unchanged.
Produce a checklist of mismatches and unresolved questions.
Require a workflow owner to inspect backups and approve any real edit.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic cases, flag any unintended changed node, connection, identity, or setting and never mark a real workflow safe based only on the generated checklist.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A workflow owner supplies authorized exports and verifies backups, concurrency, version behavior, and every change. The proposal does not edit or activate a workflow, and real changes require access and permission.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports n8n version locking, node restoration, or safe workflow edits.
The retained spans do not establish a verified concurrency guard or API behavior.
Checklist accuracy on real workflows and any buyer willingness to pay are unknown.

ease.reason: A student can compare fictional state descriptions, but the post's version-specific n8n repair mechanics have no supplied implementation support.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: n8n consultants may pay for repair preparation; this request establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week text-only checklist prototype is bounded; actual node restoration, concurrency safety, and version-specific behavior remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed tool can compare supplied descriptions, but a qualified person must inspect backups and authorize every real workflow change.

evidence.reason: The retained spans specify one missing node, two connections, and invariants to preserve, but provide no implementation reference or verified safe repair method.

candidates.reason: The retained spans support a specific repair-planning chore and a checklist experiment using synthetic descriptions. The provisional mean is 4.2, below threshold; no software capability establishes safe execution.

candidates.title: Queue laboratory batch records for review

demandEvidence.chore: Automate handling of the high-frequency batch records generated by laboratory testing instruments in industrial chemical manufacturing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: laboratory testing instruments generate high-frequency batch records that require automated

experimentPlan.output: A chronological review queue that groups operator-supplied synthetic batch records and flags records missing operator-defined required values.
inputs: Synthetic batch record rows supplied by an operator
Operator-defined list of fields required for the test
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a set of synthetic batch records and a test-specific list of required fields.
steps: Accept only synthetic or otherwise authorized test records.
Apply the operator's declared grouping label and required-field list.
Check each supplied record for missing declared values.
Arrange records and flagged omissions in chronological order.
Show the source values and reason for each flag to an operator.
Require an operator to confirm every flag before any operational use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On synthetic examples with operator-declared required fields, the queue lists all supplied records in timestamp order and flags only records with a missing declared value.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator must define the fields and grouping rules, provide authorized or fictional test inputs, validate every flag against the actual laboratory procedure, and approve any operational use; the prototype makes no quality or release decision.
unverified: The retained excerpt does not specify batch fields, validation rules, instruments, output format, or the requested automation mechanism.
No supplied building reference supports instrument ingestion, laboratory-system integration, or record persistence.
Frequency beyond the source's high-frequency description, access permissions, privacy requirements, and willingness to pay are unknown.

ease.reason: A student can prototype checks on supplied synthetic rows, but field rules and instrument ingestion are unspecified and unsupported.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: industrial laboratory service providers may pay for record triage; the post establishes a chore, not buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic review queue is bounded, but domain rules, instrument formats, and real data access remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: The proposed queue can apply declared missing-field checks, while a laboratory operator must define rules and verify every flag; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The fresh excerpt identifies high-frequency instrument-generated batch records requiring automation, but omits the fields, checks, output, and corroboration.

candidates.reason: The assigned post supports recurring high-frequency batch-record handling and a narrow synthetic review-queue experiment. Its provisional mean is 3.8, below six; the source omits task details and no implementation reference supports instrument integration.
